title: Characteristic of a field
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field]. There is a unique ring homomorphism $\mathbf Z\to k$, $n\mapsto n\cdot1_k$; its kernel is an ideal of $\mathbf Z$, hence of the form $p\mathbf Z$ for a unique integer $p\ge0$. This $p$ is the *characteristic* of $k$, written $\operatorname{char}k$: thus for every integer $n\ge0$ one has $n\cdot1_k=0$ if and only if $p$ divides $n$. One says $k$ has *characteristic $0$* if $p=0$ (no positive multiple of $1_k$ vanishes), and *characteristic $p>0$* otherwise, in which case $p$ is the least integer $n\ge1$ with $n\cdot 1_k=0$.
